hook_text: Hot and wet every day. Hot with a dry winter. Hot summer, mild winter. Cool and drizzly. Which is which?
clip_script: Start at the equator in the Congo: about twenty-six degrees every month and storms most afternoons. Tropical rainforest. Move away a little: still hot, but now a wet summer and a long dry winter, grass and scattered acacias, elephants and zebras. Tropical savanna. Keep going to Durban: hot, humid summers, mild winters, sugar cane on the hills. Humid subtropical. Jump to London: cool summers, chilly winters, light rain in every month. Temperate oceanic. Four climates, sorted by two things: how hot, and when it rains. And one twist: Johannesburg sits in the subtropical belt, but at one thousand seven hundred and fifty metres up, its climate is temperate.
visual_style: A whiteboard globe with a dotted line running from the equator to Durban and then jumping to London, with a tiny climate graph popping up at each stop.
pacing: Quick stops, one beat per climate, then a twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort the world's climates yourself.
